chunks: Then he was picked up by the family of Pharaoh, that he might become for them an enemy and a cause of grief. Indeed, Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers were habitual sinners.

key_terms.هَامَانَ: Haman, a high official in Pharaoh's court

ai.seo_question: Who picked up Moses and why did it become a source of regret for Pharaoh?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the divine irony of Pharaoh's household adopting the very child destined to dismantle their empire, illustrating the concept of *Hikmah* (divine wisdom) in apparent chaos. The mention of Haman alongside Pharaoh emphasizes the completeness of their leadership structure—political and administrative—yet their collective error (*Khata'*) underscores that power without divine guidance leads to inevitable ruin.
